messages:
mira-docs: Quick discovery in onboarding QA: our CLI "quickstart init" templates emit different auth header examples per language. Curl shows `Authorization: Bearer`, Python shows `Authorization: Bearer`, but Ruby template still prints `X-API-Key: <token>`. Users copy the Ruby snippet and paste into curl and get 401s.

oliver-cli: Oh no, that slipped through when we patched the hosted API. The CLI templates live in `templates/quickstart/*`. We intended a single canonical header but left a legacy Ruby template. I'll patch the generator to canonicalize the header and add a per-language mapping for idiomatic config keys.

pat-support: A couple of customers filed "auth mismatch" tickets. They were confused because the docs show one header and their language example used a different env var name (eg `REDWOOD_API_KEY` vs `REDWOOD_KEY`). Recommend we standardize env var naming in the README and then show per-language aliases.

sam-ci: I'll add two checks: (1) a docs lint rule that fails if a codeblock with language "powershell" contains single quotes around header lines, and (2) a smoke test that generates a sample from the CLI template and asserts the curl snippet contains `Authorization: Bearer`. That should catch regressions.

mira-docs: Also please add a short compatibility blurb in the README: "Legacy integrations may accept X-API-Key header. We recommend Authorization: Bearer for new integrations." Small note about key rotation and header case-insensitivity.

oliver-cli: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/pull/224 — updates templates, adds alias mapping for env var names, and tweaks the new quickstart generator tests.

lint-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1422 for adding the header/header-name lint and the PowerShell quoting rule. Assigned to @sam-ci.

pat-support: Once merged can we push a short message to #onboarding and update the quickstart snippet in the self-serve signup email? The email still embeds the old Ruby snippet.

mira-docs: Will do. Thanks everyone — should cut down on the "it works locally, fails in CI" support noise. :thumbsup:
